recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. In other words, LotusWei Elixirs help me be a better podcaster and Biofield Tuner. Benefits accumulate over long term use!

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.
recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Name: Clive de Carle

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

rec9gM6sh7SX9iOOH.Bio: Jenny Rivers is a multi-modality therapist, energy worker, and "wisdom keeper" of the female body and its cycles, discussing wombcraft, bodywork, and natural rhythms on InnerVerse.
rec9gM6sh7SX9iOOH.Name: Jenny Rivers

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Diet as an ongoing experiment", "body": "Jenny describes nine months of mostly steak, eggs and bacon, a slide back into summer fruit, sugar and holiday cookies, and a return to strict carnivore on December 26th that she says no longer works the way it first did. Chance recounts five years as a vegan that, he says, left him plateaued in climbing and lifting until he added eggs and chicken. Jenny sorts people into moderators and abstainers and finds freedom in restriction, and Chance agrees, citing his own long choice to skip dairy. Both treat the body as dynamic: listen, adjust, and never lock into dogma."}, {"title": "The ethics of eating anything at all", "body": "Jenny asks whether any being can live without killing another, arguing that plants have consciousness too and relaying the carnivore community's view that plants defend themselves with chemicals while fruit is offered to spread seed. She describes hunting in older cultures as a sacred agreement between hunter and animal, and argues that tilling and fertilizing fields treats the earth like a body forced to grow what we choose. Chance points to permaculture food forests as a gentler model, wonders whether eating farmed animals mirrors humans being farmed on a larger scale, and later says gratitude for the whole supply chain is what his earlier diets lacked."}, {"title": "Belief as the limit of human potential", "body": "Chance describes listening to the Ringing Cedars of Russia series, whose central character lives lightly clothed in the Siberian woods while squirrels bring her nuts and mushrooms, and ties it to his own barefoot walks in the snow. He argues that our bodily capacities are bounded mostly by belief and by generations spent in survival mode, and that as survival pressure eases we may find a new harmony with nature. Jenny adds a fasting book she just finished, including an account she recalls of someone going 382 days without eating, and wonders aloud what becomes possible when we choose what to believe."}, {"title": "Integrity, attention and acting as if", "body": "Jenny tells how she left a wellness center she had worked at for four years when a mask rule returned, calling integrity the alignment of inner values with outer action, and started her own women's circle. She spent December away from the news, wrestled with whether that was spiritual bypassing, and then felt, like Theoden hearing Aragorn in The Lord of the Rings, that open war was upon her anyway. Chance answers with a chameleon card about acting as if, balanced by naming what we do not consent to, and argues the most persuasive thing anyone can do is live their healthiest, strongest life."}, {"title": "Wombcraft and the wisdom of cycles", "body": "Jenny's wombcraft mentoring walks women through the four phases of the menstrual cycle, which she pairs with the maiden, mother, wild woman and crone archetypes, and which she says the medical system surrounds with myths. She frames the wild woman phase before bleeding not as a stigma about hormonal women but as a rightful need to rage and speak out against what we no longer stand for, a Kali kind of energy. Her larger point is that everyone moves through cycles, and that the more we honor them, the more we can transcend them toward the calm, unchanging part of us."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Jenny Rivers is a multi-modality therapist, energy worker, and wisdom keeper of the female body and it's cycles. She joins me for a multifaceted flow state where we chat on diet and the many "isms" around food, recovering from the winter-season funk, and her offerings as a healer and teacher, such as bodywork practices and knowledge of human biological rhythms.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the Plus+ Extension we talk about tracking heavenly cycles, deconstructing mythological archetypes, what Imbolc means in nature, Michael Wann the synchronicity-generator, fusing various movement medicine traditions, and much more.
